messages.subject: count data, heat map
parts:
I am creating a graph that uses a heat map like display to show the percentage of samples that are recorded with different values in several categories.  To do this I am using the stat_bin2d() which gives me most everything that I want.  However, I have noticed the placement of the bins is dependent on the other values in a group.  For instance in the graph produced with the code below groups A and C should have equal overlap with group B but they don't.  So what am I doing wrong?  If anybody has a suggestion of a fix or a different approach for this type of graph I would be very appreciative.


mt <- as.data.frame(matrix(rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 10), 30, 2))
mt[, 2] <- c(rep(18, 5), rep(20, 5), rep(20, 10), rep(20, 5), rep(22,5))
colnames(mt) <- c("group", "count")
ggplot(data=mt,aes(x=mt$count, y=mt$group)) + stat_bin2d(binwidth = c(1, .5))


cheers

Heath

messages.subject: Re: count data, heat map
parts:
Hi:

This is a different way to attack the problem, via geom_tile().

mt <- as.data.frame(matrix(rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 10), 30, 2))
mt[, 2] <- c(rep(18, 5), rep(20, 5), rep(20, 10), rep(20, 5), rep(22,5))
colnames(mt) <- c("group", "count")

# geom_tile() likes factors for the x and y variables, so convert
count to factor
mt$count <- factor(mt$count)

# Use plyr to get frequencies of the group * count combinations and use
# the frequency var as the fill aesthetic in geom_tile()
library(plyr)
mt2 <- ddply(mt, .(group, count), summarise, freq = length(count))

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mt2, aes(y = group, x = count, fill = freq)) + geom_tile()

If you prefer to have a legend with values 5 and 10 rather than the
colorbar, then convert freq to be factor as well.

Dennis
